These can be represented as directed edges in a graph where an edge \(X \to Y\) denotes that \(X\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) (equivalently, \(Y\) is a descendant of \(X\)). Because the ancestor-descendant relation is transitive, the existence of a path from \(A\) to \(B\) establishes that \(A\) is an ancestor of \(B\).

- Christian \(\to\) Virginia
- Katherine \(\to\) Alexis

Extend the first chain by successively appending every statement whose left-hand side matches the current right-most individual:
Christian \(\to\) Virginia \(\to\) Melissa \(\to\) Jeremy \(\to\) Billy \(\to\) Judith \(\to\) Vincent \(\to\) Nathan \(\to\) … (continuing through 70+ additional links) … \(\to\) Christine \(\to\) Nancy.

The second chain is likewise extended:
Nancy \(\to\) Ashley \(\to\) Bryan \(\to\) Elijah \(\to\) Grace \(\to\) Lawrence \(\to\) Lori \(\to\) Jacob \(\to\) Jeffrey \(\to\) Emily \(\to\) Peter \(\to\) Doris \(\to\) Nicholas \(\to\) Samantha \(\to\) Richard \(\to\) Hannah \(\to\) Karen \(\to\) Roy \(\to\) Steven \(\to\) Terry \(\to\) Angela \(\to\) Willie \(\to\) Gloria \(\to\) Timothy \(\to\) Madison \(\to\) Kimberly \(\to\) Katherine \(\to\) Alexis.

Because the extended Christian-chain ends at Nancy and the Alexis-chain begins at Nancy, the two chains concatenate. The resulting composite path is
Christian \(\to\) … \(\to\) Nancy \(\to\) … \(\to\) Alexis.
Hence Christian is an ancestor of Alexis, which means Alexis is a descendant of Christian. This matches option 1; none of the other options is required once a direct ancestor-descendant link has been established.
